Yes—Entire Graph already has five tailored runners: summary, semantic diff, review, risk, and security. ForgeMark should use the broader CLI/Entire.io set, plus one benchmark-specific monitor.

## Recommended ForgeMark set

| Runner | Purpose | ForgeMark-specific focus |
|---|---|---|
| `trail-summary` | Reviewer overview | Explain the workload, protocol, CLI, schema, or frontend behavior changed. |
| `trail-semantic-diff` | Structured change narrative | Group changes into engine, Git transport/auth, statistics/results, and frontend/CLI pages. |
| `trail-review-focus` | Point reviewers at critical files | Credential paths, goroutines, push/delete operations, statistics, result schemas, and CI. |
| `trail-review` | Inline defect findings | Concurrency leaks, cancellation bugs, incorrect Git refs, credential exposure, misleading metrics, and compatibility regressions. |
| `trail-risk` | Blast-radius score | Accidental forge load, destructive remote writes, benchmark invalidation, public CLI/schema changes, and cross-forge behavior. |
| `trail-security` | Adversarial security score | Token leakage, hostile URLs/redirects, TLS bypass, proxy behavior, dependency changes, and auth-token audience mistakes. |
| `trail-confidence` | Correctness confidence score | Race coverage, concurrent failure paths, all four strategies, HTTP mocks, result compatibility, and CI gate coverage. |
| `trail-drift` | Architectural alignment score | Keep `internal/bench` frontend-neutral, `internal/results` as schema owner, the CLI thin, and real Git operations—not synthetic HTTP. |
| `trail-benchmark-fidelity` | **Custom high-value monitor** | Ask whether results still mean what they claim: warm-up exclusion, successful-op denominators, percentiles, read/write separation, independent refs, and non-perturbing sinks. |

The custom monitor should probably be:

```text
key: fidelity
label: Benchmark Fidelity
value_type: percent
polarity: higher_is_better
```

That monitor is especially valuable because ForgeMark’s central contract is measurement validity. The sensitive invariants are visible in [stats.go](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/forgemark/internal/bench/stats.go:27), while its workload semantics live in [config.go](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/forgemark/internal/bench/config.go:37).

- Treat `{{branch}}` and `{{base_branch}}` as untrusted, following Entire Graph’s hardened ref-handling pattern.
- Never run a live ForgeMark benchmark or contact an external forge during evaluation.
- Use only repository inspection and local unit/race/lint checks.
- Preserve the legacy and normalized result contracts in [results.go](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/forgemark/internal/results/results.go:1).
- Treat credentials and token refresh behavior in [creds.go](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/forgemark/internal/bench/creds.go:44) as high-risk.
- Explicitly consider the authorized-load-testing warning and destructive traffic model documented in the [README](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/forgemark/README.md:17).

content.text:
Yes. Entire supports a dedicated private checkpoint repository while the source repository remains public.

For example:

```bash
entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:entireio/forgemark-checkpoints
git add .entire/settings.json
git commit -m "Configure private checkpoint remote"
```

Create `entireio/forgemark-checkpoints` as a private repository first.

Important caveats:

- Keep the checkpoint repo under the same owner as the code repo; cross-owner configurations are rejected as fork protection.
- Commit `.entire/settings.json` so Entire.io can discover the external repository.
- Install/authorize the Entire GitHub App on the private checkpoint repo so Entire.io can read it.
- The public settings file will reveal the private repository’s name, but not its contents.
- This redirects checkpoint branches/refs only; it does not redirect code or trail branches.
- If checkpoints were previously pushed to the public repo, configuring this only affects future pushes. The existing public `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch or `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` must be handled separately.

The behavior is documented in [README.md](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/cli/README.md:385), and Entire.io explicitly resolves external checkpoint repositories from committed settings in [checkpoint-detection.ts](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/entire.io/api/src/lib/checkpoint-detection.ts:1).

I found the blocker: the push succeeded, but it intentionally did not create a branch.

### Findings

1. **[P1] `git-refs` is incompatible with the intended workflow**

   [.entire/settings.json line 20](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/blob/f15f5337f89c32014de1f15ab9ed9dc34d159e73/.entire/settings.json#L17-L21) selects:

   ```json
   "checkpoints": {
     "primary": {
       "type": "git-refs"
     }
   }
   ```

   That stores checkpoints under:

   ```text
   refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<checkpoint-id>
   ```

   These are custom Git refs—not `refs/heads/*` branches—so GitHub’s Branches page will not display them. The screenshot’s wording, `Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s)`, confirms this path was used. The CLI prints `done` only after Git accepts the push ([manual_commit_push.go](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:343)).

   More importantly, current Entire.io ingestion only recognizes `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` ([checkpoint-storage.ts](/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/entire.io/api/src/lib/checkpoint-storage.ts:7)). It will ignore the custom checkpoint ref even though it reached GitHub.

   **Fix:** remove the entire `checkpoints` block. The CLI defaults to the supported `git-branch` backend:

   ```json
   {
     "enabled": true,
     "strategy_options": {
       "checkpoint_remote": {
         "provider": "github",
         "repo": "ohcnetwork/care_fe-checkpoints"
       },
       "push_sessions": true
     },
     "redaction": {
       "pii": {
         "enabled": true,
         "email": true,
         "phone": true,
         "address": true
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. **[P3] Contributors without Entire are not completely unaffected**

   The PR description says contributors without the CLI are unaffected, but the [Codex SessionStart hook](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/blob/f15f5337f89c32014de1f15ab9ed9dc34d159e73/.codex/hooks.json#L19-L23) injects an installation warning into every Codex session. If silent opt-out is intended, it should exit without printing, like the other hooks.

### Before retesting

- Merge the checkpoint configuration into the default `develop` branch; Entire.io discovers the external remote from committed default-branch settings.
- Ensure the Entire GitHub App has access to the private checkpoint repository.
- Create a new checkpoint after switching back to `git-branch`; the already-pushed custom ref will not automatically become a branch.
- The existing hidden ref can be confirmed from the contributor’s authenticated machine:

  ```bash
  git ls-remote git@github.com:ohcnetwork/care_fe-checkpoints.git \
    'refs/entire/checkpoints/*'
  ```

My GitHub account cannot access the private checkpoint repo—it returns 404—so I couldn’t list that ref directly. I did not submit a GitHub review.
